title: Check whether my account is allowed to use sudo
summary: Ask sudo which administrator commands your user may run. It asks for your own password and only prints the list, so nothing on the system is changed.

aliases.text: am I allowed to use sudo
what can I run with sudo
есть ли у меня доступ к sudo
что я могу делать через sudo

steps.explain: Show the groups your user belongs to. Admin rights usually come from a group: sudo on Debian, Ubuntu and Mint, wheel on Fedora and openSUSE, admin on macOS. Being in the group is not proof, so check with the next step.
steps.expect: One line of group names, for example: t sudo. Note whether sudo, wheel or admin is in the list.

steps.explain: Ask sudo which commands your user may run with administrator rights. It asks for your own password (typing stays hidden) and only prints the list. If you see 'command not found', sudo is not installed here.
steps.expect: Allowed: 'User <name> may run the following commands on <host>:' then lines like '(ALL : ALL) ALL'. Not allowed: 'Sorry, user <name> may not run sudo on <host>.'

warnings: On Arch Linux the wheel group is off by default, so a wheel member can still see 'may not run sudo'. Trust the sudo -l output, not the group name.
